body: In Rune 0.1.60.

body: In Rune 0.1.60.

title: Export painted iPhone buttons for native activation
body: In Rune 0.1.60.

title: Rework iPhone terminal input and session switching
body: In Rune 0.1.60.

title: Developer mode and labs, feature flags every client and the server read
body: In Rune 0.1.60.

title: Frost sessions in place and swipe between tabs before sessions
body: In Rune 0.1.60.

title: Clearer search feedback
body: In Rune 0.1.59: Sessions keeps no-match feedback compact, with a hint to try another name or clear the search.

title: Phone navigation, within reach
body: In Rune 0.1.58: swipe between sessions or pull Sessions in from the left edge. Return stays in reach and Shift keeps text selection local. Reconnecting cancels unfinished drags.

title: Attach photos and files on iPhone
body: The paperclip on the iOS key bar sends photos, files and pasted images to the pane you're in.

title: Every paired computer on your phone
body: Rune on iPhone keeps every computer you've paired; tap one to switch between them.

title: A tidier sidebar
body: Your work sits in compact rows, local first. Only real splits get layered edges, with their panes listed inline.

title: Links open where you are
body: Click a link in a remote pane and it opens on the computer in front of you, not the one running the pane.

title: Scrollback survives a restart
body: Restart the phux server and your panes come back with their history.

title: Rune is the iPhone app
body: The phone app now runs Rune: a continuous navigator replaces session cards, and the terminal runs edge to edge.

title: A theme per machine
body: Give a host its own theme and Rune wears it while you're on that host, so you always know where you're typing.

title: Child panes fold under their parent
body: Panes an agent spawns remember who started them and tuck under it in the sidebar.

title: phux:// links and keep-awake
body: phux:// links open sessions, tabs, folders and exact panes. Keep-awake shows in the sidebar and switches from the palette.

title: One list of work
body: The sidebar and the tab strip show the same list, in the same order.

title: Pane numbers, synced typing, copy-mode search
body: Jump to a pane by number, type into several at once, search in copy mode, and option-click to place the cursor.

title: Liquid glass on the phone
body: The phone layout gets native liquid glass and a careful pass over every bar and sheet.

title: Tabs inside a split
body: ⌘⇧←/→ moves between tabs in a split, a 2/3 badge shows where you are, and dropping a terminal on a pane makes it a tab there.

title: Kitty images and region screenshots
body: Rune draws Kitty graphics, and you can screenshot a region of the screen straight into the focused agent's pane.

title: Interface size and clickable paths
body: Scale the chrome without touching the terminal font, and ⌘-click a file path printed in a pane to open it.

title: Quick Look, Finder and Handoff
body: Quick Look files from a pane, open folders in Rune from Finder, and hand the pane in front to your iPhone.

title: Set up from the window
body: Rune installs phux when it's missing, pairs your phone from Settings, and adds your other machines from ssh config.

title: A Windows 98 theme, previewed as you browse
body: Windows 98 joins the themes: silver, navy and the old VGA colours. In the palette, a highlighted theme shows live as you move through the results; Return keeps it and Escape puts yours back.

title: Tabs that make room
body: Tabs share the title bar instead of running under its buttons: a crowd narrows the resting ones and the active tab keeps its name. Hover a tab to close it, or rest on any button to see what it does and its keys.

title: Pair your phone by scanning
body: Pairing the phone client starts with the camera: scan the code and you're in, no typing an address.

title: Kitchen, pit lane, pitch and hive
body: Four new playground views from the palette. Every agent is a chef, a car, a player or a bee; one that needs you says so, and a press shows its terminal. Escape or the esc chip closes any of them.

title: Screen mirrors on demand
body: List a machine's screens and start a mirror when you want one, and trade clipboards between a viewer and the mirrored host.

title: Release channels in Settings
body: About & Updates picks Stable or Next for the local phux, and Linux gets the same settings as macOS.

title: A signed Mac app and Linux arm64
body: Rune ships as a signed DMG, and Linux builds now cover arm64 as well as x86_64.

title: Satellite sessions in the sidebar
body: A hub lists its satellites' sessions and mirrors alongside its own, so another machine's work is one click away.

title: Reef, galaxy and creatures
body: The fleet as a reef or a galaxy, with creatures that grow as your agents get work done.

title: Answer agents from the inbox
body: ACP agent questions show up in the inbox, even ones asked before Rune connected, and you answer them right there.
